Twenty Sixth Indian Antarctic Expedition 2006-2008
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 24, pp 313-319
Studies on Seismotectonics and Geodynamical
Processes Between Antarctica and  India —
Observations from Maitri, Antarctica
G. S. Srinivas
National Geophysical Research Institute, Hyderabad
A. Operation of Seismological Observatory at Maitri
B. Permanent GPS tracking station at Maitri
SEISMOLOGICAL OBSERV ATORY AT MAITRI, ANTARCTICA
INTRODUCTION
Antarctica is one of the stable continents in the world and so
seismic activity is very low and crustal deformation is highly precise. In
order to monitor the seismic activity in and around Antarctica and the
Indian Ocean region, a permanent Digital Seismological Station was
installed during the 17
th Indian Antarctic Expedition and was fully
commissioned in 1998.
OBJECTIVE
Establishment of the seismic station with high-resolution digital
seismic equipment as well as an analog seismic recorder to monitor the
seismic activity in and around Antarctica.
Monitoring of tele-seismic activity as well as the activity in mid
oceanic ridges in the Indian Ocean Region.
METHODOLOGY AND RESULTS
A thermally insulated vault was fabricated by R & D Engineers,
DRDO, Pune. An underground pit was dug and the vault was buried in
the pit. An electronically controlled temperature sensor was installed in
the seismic vault, to maintain the temperature at 15º C. As there was
seepage of water due to snow/ice melting during summer period, which
314
would affect the instruments, the complete concrete base was redone and
a pier was constructed. Later, the Short period system, which was not
functioning properly was removed along with the Seismometers, Cables
and back loaded. The observatory was upgraded with GEOTECH
Broadband system- KS-2000M, together with Smart 24R Digitizer in 25
th
IAE. A GPS clock has been augmented with the system for accurate
time. High quality, uninterrupted three component digital data was
collected. A vertical component analog Seismometer-Model-S-13 of
Teledyne Geotech make is also being operated simultaneously. Recording
is done with RV320R Portacorder.  The data collected during 26
th IAE,
2006-2007 have been analyzed. A total number of 647 earthquakes were
recorded that includes both seismic activities in and around Antarctica
and also global seismic events which have been recorded and shown in
Epimap of the global earthquakes. Most of the earthquakes were tele-seismic.
Few regional earthquakes with epicenter in Indian Ocean were recorded.
The recently updated Seismic station at Maitri is continuously
operational and is as shown in Figure 1. The digital seismic data
acquired using Geotech broadband KS-2000M Seismometer and Smart
24R Digitizer during 26
th IAE, 2007 have been analyzed. A total number
of 647 earthquakes were recorded, that includes both the seismic activities
